rationales: J.J. Thomson proposed the plum-pudding model, not electron orbits.
Rutherford proposed a nuclear model but did not use Bohr's quantized orbits.
Planck introduced the quantum theory, not the concept of atomic orbits.
Bohr used the concept of fixed electron orbits around the nucleus.
Mendeleev's postulate was the basis of the earlier periodic table, not the long-form table.
The long-form periodic table is arranged according to increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the basis for constructing the modern long-form periodic table.
Mass number is not the basis for arranging elements in the long-form periodic table.
m/m percent requires the mass of the solute and mass of the solution.
m/v percent requires the mass of the solute and volume of the solution.
The solute is given by volume and the solvent by mass, so this is v/m percent.
v/v percent requires both solute and solution amounts to be expressed by volume.
Metallic bonding involves attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons, not electron transfer between atoms.
Electron transfer between atoms forms oppositely charged ions and an ionic bond.
Covalent bonding forms by sharing electrons rather than transferring them.
Coordinate covalent bonding forms when one atom supplies both shared electrons.
A covalent bond pair does not consist of only one electron.
A covalent bond pair consists of two shared electrons.
Three electrons do not make a bond pair.
Four electrons do not make a single bond pair.
Molecules with very low energy are unlikely to escape the liquid surface.
Molecules escaping by evaporation generally have more than moderate energy.
The molecules that escape the surface have relatively high kinetic energy.
This is incorrect because evaporating molecules have high kinetic energy.
Sugar solution does not produce ions in water and is a non-electrolyte.
Sulphuric acid solution produces ions and conducts electricity.
Lime solution contains ions and can conduct electricity.
Sodium chloride solution dissociates into ions and conducts electricity.
Some metals form unipositive ions, such as sodium ions.
Some metals form dipositive ions, such as magnesium ions.
Some metals form tripositive ions, such as aluminium ions.
Metals can form ions with all these charges.
A molecular formula gives the actual number of each type of atom in a molecule.
Formula mass is the sum of the atomic masses in a formula unit.
Chemical formula is a general representation and need not show the simplest ratio.
An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.
Fluorine's atomic number is not 5; that is boron's atomic number.
Fluorine's atomic number is not 7; that is nitrogen's atomic number.
Fluorine has atomic number 9.
Fluorine's atomic number is not 15; that is phosphorus's atomic number.
The s subshell is not the subshell being filled in transition elements.
The p subshell is not the subshell being filled in transition elements.
Transition elements have a d subshell in the process of filling.
The f subshell is filled in inner-transition elements, not the usual transition elements.
Size is not the specific term for half the internuclear distance between bonded atoms.
Shielding effect describes the reduction in nuclear attraction by inner electrons.
An orbit is a region or path associated with an electron, not this distance.
Atomic radius is conventionally half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded identical atoms.
An ionic bond involves electron transfer, not equal sharing.
A coordinate bond forms when one atom contributes both shared electrons.
A polar covalent bond involves unequal sharing of the electron pair.
Equal sharing between similar atoms forms a pure covalent bond.
Lone is not the nature of van der Waals forces.
Liquid describes a state of matter, not the nature of these forces.
Chemical is too broad and does not describe the forces' physical origin.
Van der Waals forces arise from electrical attractions between molecules or particles.
Evaporation is the change from liquid to gas.
Melting is the change from solid to liquid.
Transpiration is water loss from plants, not gas changing to liquid.
Condensation is the change from gas phase to liquid.
